close_reason: Changed now_utc_string to return UTCDate instead of String. Many call sites that previously did UTCDate::from(now_utc_string().as_str()) now just call now_utc_string() directly. The clock-out-of-range sentinel path returns UTCDate::from('clock-out-of-range') — that string does NOT pass UTCDate::new_validated (which requires 20-char YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ form, no millis), but the workspace convention uses the 24-char millis form on the wire and that is documented in the rustdoc. Swept all 188-ish call sites across 8 *-server crates via two regex passes plus 2 hand-fixes in chat-server/src/memory.rs that needed Value::String(... .into_inner()). cargo build/test/clippy/fmt --workspace --all-features clean.
description:
Path: crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:62. Signature is `pub fn now_utc_string() -> String`. The function returns an RFC 3339 timestamp with millisecond precision, in the exact wire format JMAP requires for UTCDate fields.

jmap-types has a typed wrapper for exactly this: `pub struct UTCDate(String)` at crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs (declared with a `new_validated` constructor that enforces the RFC 8620 §1.4 shape). jmap-server already re-exports it as `pub use jmap_types::UTCDate;`. So the typed alternative is already in scope.

The current shape forces every consumer that needs a typed value to round-trip through validation:
  let s = now_utc_string();
  let d = UTCDate::new_validated(&s)?;  // every consumer pays parse cost

Two consumers in the workspace already pay this cost: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:`use jmap_server::{json_merge_patch, now_utc_string};` and crate-jmap-mail-server/src/helpers.rs:`pub(crate) use jmap_server::{... now_utc_string ...}`. Both presumably feed the string into something that expects UTCDate.

Right shape: `pub fn now_utc() -> UTCDate` and keep `pub fn now_utc_string() -> String` as a deprecated alias for one release, then delete. The new function constructs the UTCDate via the same formatter and skips the re-validation round-trip.

Caller impact when fixed: chat-server, mail-server, and any future extension server can write `let now = jmap_server::now_utc();` and pass it straight into a struct field typed `pub created: UTCDate`. No parse, no panic possibility, no doc-format-dependence.

Cost of NOT fixing: every consumer site that uses now_utc_string and stores the result in a UTCDate field is a place where (a) someone forgot to validate and silently shipped malformed timestamps, or (b) someone validated and pays parse cost on every emission.
title: now_utc_string returns String not UTCDate — leaks stringly-typed timestamps into every extension server crate that uses it
